newsitem.title: UK: BASS shares slip after final results.
newsitem.headline: BASS shares slip after final results.

text.p: Shares in brewer-to-leisure group Bass Plc fell in pre-market trade on Wednesday after the company reported a 12 percent increase in annual profits but gave no news on the proposed Carlsberg-Tetley acquisition plans.
The shares were off 3p to 808p by 0831 GMT after closing 17p firmer on Tuesday in anticipation of favourable results.
Pre-tax profits came in at 671 million stg compared with analysts forecasts of between 665-675 million stg and 599 million stg reported a year earlier.
The dividend was raised to 25p, beating most analysts expectations.
Charles Winston, analyst at BZW, said Bass had reported "a very strong set of figures and very strong cashflow."

But the shares suffered from a bit of profit-taking after Tuesday's strong gains and were depressed by the generally weaker stock market. The Dow's sharp decline overnight dragged 80 percent of FTSE stocks lower on Wednesday.
Bass chairman Sir Ian Prosser said the company planned to spend 670 million stg on the business next year, creating some 7,000 jobs.
"They had already flagged the investment," said Winston. "It was pretty much in line with what we expected."
Prosser added that the company expected "continued buoyancy in UK consumer spending over the next year."

But analysts were also hoping for a statement on the proposed 200 million stg Carlsberg-Tetley deal, which recent newspaper reports have suggested may be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
"There is no news on Carlsberg-Tetley which people were hoping for," Winston said. "That will continue to dog the share price."
